newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM pledges support for Fujimori's speech. [CORRECTED 13:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Japan PM pledges support for Fujimori's speech. [CORRECTED 13:05 GMT]

text.p: Japan Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto (corrects from Peru Prime Minister) said on Sunday Japan would support Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori's speech to Marxist rebels holding 340 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
"Japan supports President (Alberto) Fujimori's televised message to the nation," Hashimoto told reporters.
Hashimoto was speaking after talking by telephone with Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda who held his second meeting with the Peruvian leader in Lima.

In a blunt speech broadcast on local television and radio late on Saturday, Fujimori said a non-violent "way out" would be possible if the rebels surrendered weapons and released their roughly 340 hostages.

"The proposal is concrete: that the captors surrender their weapons to a guarantor committee and that they allow of all the hostages without exception," Fujimori said. "In this way the possibility of force being used by the Peruvian state will be ruled out and from there, with all guarantees, a way out can be studied."

The speech, which Fujimori read in a rapid, stern voice, was his first public statement since the crisis began on Tuesday when about 20 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels stormed an exclusive cocktail party at the residence.
